chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and Abū Dāwūd together, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
If you have performed part of your wudu (ablution), then some need arises for you such that your wudu dries, then repeat your wudu, for wudu is not to be divided.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution) as the ritual act under discussion
key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: a need or intervening matter that interrupts the act
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ: then repeat; perform it again from the beginning
key_terms.لَا يُبَعَّضُ: it is not divided; it is not to be performed in disconnected portions
key_terms.وُضُوئِكَ: your wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for prayer
key_terms.يَبِسَ: it dried up; the moisture of the wudu ceased

ai.seo_question: If my wudu dries before I finish it, do I need to repeat the entire wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning continuity in wudu (ablution). It states that if a person interrupts wudu and the moisture dries before completion, the wudu must be redone because wudu is not to be performed in separated parts.
